record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: Is there a universal decay rate for the long-time survival probability in generic open billiards with mixed phase space, where typical trajectories may be regular or chaotic depending on initial condition and sticky motion near elliptic islands is conjectured in area-preserving maps to produce algebraic survival decay with a universal exponent?

evidence.quote: Typical billiards are expected to have mixed phase space, that is, chaotic or regular depending on the initial condition
Open problem 10. Is there a universal decay rate in generic open billiards?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an open billiard in the plane (or on a surface), i.e., a domain $\Omega$ with piecewise smooth boundary in which a point particle moves in straight lines and reflects elastically from $\partial\Omega$, together with a designated "hole" $H \subset \partial\Omega$ (or an open subregion of phase space) through which the particle escapes. The survival probability is
$$P(t) = \mu\{(q,v) \in \Omega \times S^1 : \text{the trajectory starting from }(q,v)\text{ has not entered }H\text{ by time }t\},$$
where $\mu$ is the natural (Liouville) invariant measure on the phase space.

Call a billiard "generic with mixed phase space" if its phase space decomposes into invariant regions of chaotic motion together with KAM-type elliptic islands surrounded by invariant tori, and if the boundary of the chaotic component carries the hallmarks of sticky dynamics (a hierarchical island-around-island structure causing arbitrarily long but finite trapping times of chaotic trajectories near regular regions). For area-preserving smooth maps it is conjectured that, due to such sticky motion near elliptic islands, the long-time survival probability decays algebraically,
$$P(t) \sim C\, t^{-\gamma}\qquad (t \to \infty),$$
with an exponent $\gamma$ that is universal (independent of the specific system within the generic mixed class).

Question: Does there exist a universal exponent $\gamma > 0$ such that for every generic open billiard with mixed phase space the survival probability $P(t)$ satisfies $P(t) \sim C\, t^{-\gamma}$ as $t \to \infty$ (with $C$ possibly depending on the billiard and the hole)? If so, determine $\gamma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of a universal algebraic decay exponent for survival in generic mixed-phase-space Hamiltonian/billiard systems remains open and actively debated. Different studies report differing power-law exponents (e.g., γ≈1 for open mushroom billiards governed by MUPOs, γ≈1.57 from island-around-island hierarchies in area-preserving maps, and other values for specific families), and recent works (2024–2025) continue to investigate scaling laws and stickiness without establishing a single universal exponent across all generic mixed billiards.

status_evidence.title: Universal exponent for transport in mixed Hamiltonian dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a universal exponent governing transport in mixed Hamiltonian systems based on island-around-island hierarchy.
status_evidence.claim: There is an ongoing conjecture/effort to identify a universal transport exponent in mixed Hamiltonian dynamics; not settled for general billiards.

status_evidence.title: From Hyperbolic to Non-Hyperbolic Open Billiards: An Entropy and Scaling Law Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) study of escape/scaling laws in open billiards, indicating the problem is still under active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on scaling laws for open billiards with mixed phase space, indicating the universality question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: An investigation of escape and scaling properties of a billiard system
status_evidence.snippet: Reports power-law tails in survival probability associated with stickiness, with system-dependent features.
status_evidence.claim: Reported decay exponents vary across systems, consistent with the universal-exponent question being unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Survival Probability for the Stadium Billiard
status_evidence.snippet: Power-law decay of survival probability tied to marginally unstable orbits, exponent depending on the model.
status_evidence.claim: Different billiard models yield different power-law exponents, no proven universal value.
